title: Fix failing fetch requests for GPIO HTTP POST

requirements.text: Fix the GPIO HTTP POST fetch calls in gpioHttp.ts so that requests to localhost:3000/gpio succeed reliably. Investigate and resolve any issues with the fetch configuration (e.g., no-cors mode preventing response inspection, incorrect headers, request body serialization, or error handling that masks the real failure). Ensure errors are surfaced with meaningful messages.
acceptanceCriteria: GPIO button controls successfully POST to localhost:3000/gpio without fetch errors in the console
The DebugHttpPanel send button successfully POST to localhost:3000/gpio and shows a success result
Network errors (e.g., server unreachable) surface a clear error message in the UI rather than silently failing
Fetch failures are reported via toast notifications so the user is aware of connection issues

requirements.text: Fix the DebugHttpPanel component so its manual send button correctly fires the HTTP POST request to localhost:3000/gpio and displays the success or failure result in the panel UI.
acceptanceCriteria: Clicking the DebugHttpPanel send button triggers a POST request to localhost:3000/gpio
The panel displays a visible success message when the request completes successfully
The panel displays a visible error message when the request fails, including the reason
The button is not permanently disabled or stuck in a loading state after a failed request

constraints: Do not modify any files under frontend/src/hooks/useInternetIdentity.ts, frontend/src/hooks/useActor.ts, frontend/src/main.tsx, or frontend/src/components/ui
The GPIO endpoint target URL (localhost:3000/gpio) must remain unchanged unless the user specifies otherwise
nonGoals: Changing the GPIO endpoint URL or port
Adding a new backend canister endpoint for HTTP proxying
Modifying the Raspberry Pi bash runner scripts
Changing the control layout or UI design
